system.system_purpose: In-product support assistant for the Relay project-management platform. Signed-in users ask questions in the help panel and receive cited answers drawn from Relay help-center documentation and their workspace's support history.

claims.value: In-product support assistant that answers signed-in users' questions from Relay documentation and the workspace's support history, with cited passages.
Available to every signed-in user of any workspace on any plan.
All workspaces are served from one shared retrieval index.
A query returns the top eight passages ranked by embedding similarity; relevance alone selects the passages that reach the prompt.
nightly
Only writer to the retrieval index.
Managed vector database holding embeddings of help-center articles and resolved support tickets.
Reachable only from the answer service's network segment.
Resolved support tickets are retained for two years and then deleted under the agreed retention schedule.
Customer email addresses are masked by the support platform before tickets appear in the resolved-tickets export.
Ticket text sometimes includes configuration snippets customers pasted into support conversations; masking covers email addresses only.
Help-center repository is public documentation.
Model provider's terms for the assistant's traffic exclude training on submitted content.
Requests to the model provider are sent over TLS.
Retrieved passages are placed inside a delimited context block; system instructions treat content inside that block as reference material, not instructions.
Answers are returned with the source reference of each cited passage.
Answers are rendered in the help panel as plain text; the panel does not execute or interpret model output.
The answer service runs as a single deployment beside the main Relay API, with a liveness probe exposed beside the Relay API.
Each answer makes one model call; there is no multi-step agent loop and the assistant takes no actions beyond returning text.
A per-workspace daily answer quota bounds spend, and the service can be disabled per workspace with a feature flag.
Answer quality is reviewed weekly via a manual sample of twenty answers by the support team.
OpenAPI declares a workspaceToken HTTP bearer security scheme applied by default to operations, representing the signed-in user's workspace-scoped session token.

A candidate record describes RetrievalIndex.search as scoring every chunk in a process-global index without an authorization scope and returning global top-k results, including private ticket chunks belonging to other workspaces.
claims.rationale: This behavior is described in an AI-generated Mantis candidate record and has not been independently verified in the provided documentation.

claims.value: A candidate record states that run_nightly updates only rows present in the current export and propagate_deletions removes content only for explicit tombstone rows, so partial or interrupted exports may leave old chunks in the index indefinitely.
claims.rationale: This ingestion behavior and its implications are described in an AI-generated Mantis candidate record rather than the primary architecture documents.

claims.value: A candidate record states that when WORKSPACE_TOKENS is unset or empty, load_settings substitutes a hard-coded mapping containing dev-token-acme and dev-token-globex, and that main.py calls load_settings at import without a development-mode gate.
claims.rationale: This configuration behavior is described in an AI-generated Mantis candidate record and is not corroborated elsewhere in the documentation.

claims.value: A candidate record describes an unauthenticated POST /admin/reindex route that calls run_nightly directly and is not declared in openapi.yaml.
claims.rationale: The endpoint is described in an AI-generated Mantis candidate record and is explicitly noted as absent from the OpenAPI specification.

claims.value: A candidate record asserts that the answer route reads the Authorization header but does not enforce the workspaceToken dependency, so requests without a valid header proceed using a default workspace despite the OpenAPI security declaration.
claims.rationale: This mismatch between declared authentication and route implementation is described only in an AI-generated Mantis candidate record.

claims.value: After each answer, provider.py posts the request identifier, the retrieved chunk text, and the generated answer to an external telemetry collector keyed by a shared collector token.
claims.rationale: This data flow is described in an AI-generated Mantis candidate record and is not mentioned in the primary architecture or operations documents.

claims.value: The Mantis security review packet and its findings and patches are automatically generated by Mantis AI and must be manually verified by an expert before deployment or disclosure; candidate records are marked PROVISIONALLY_VALID with no reproduction attempted.

components.name: Help panel
components.description: In-product chat surface in Relay where signed-in users ask support questions.

components.name: Ingestion pipeline
components.description: Nightly ingestion job that reads the published help-center repository and the support platform's resolved-tickets export, chunks and embeds content, and writes embeddings into the retrieval index.

components.name: Retrieval index
components.description: Managed vector database holding embeddings of help-center articles and resolved support tickets for all workspaces in a single shared index.

components.name: Help-center repository
components.description: Source repository of published Relay help-center documentation consumed by the ingestion pipeline.

components.name: Support platform
components.description: External support platform that stores customer support tickets and exports resolved tickets (with masked email addresses) for ingestion.

components.name: Provider wrapper (provider.py)
components.description: Internal module that orchestrates calls to the hosted model provider and posts answer telemetry, including retrieved chunk text and generated answers, to an external analytics collector.

components.name: Hosted model provider API
components.description: Hosted large-language-model API that receives the user's question and retrieved passages from the answer service.

components.name: Analytics collector
components.description: External telemetry collector at analytics.relay-answers.example that receives request identifiers, retrieved chunk text, and generated answers keyed by a shared collector token.

assets.name: Support ticket text
assets.description: Resolved customer support tickets, with customer email addresses masked before export but including free-form conversation text and configuration snippets.
assets.confidentiality_impact: Disclosure could reveal sensitive support conversations and customer configuration details.
assets.integrity_impact: Corruption or cross-workspace mixing of ticket text could misrepresent customer history and affect support decisions.
assets.availability_impact: Loss could hinder support teams' ability to reference past cases.

assets.name: Help-center content
assets.description: Public Relay help-center documentation used as a source for answers.
assets.integrity_impact: Incorrect or outdated documentation could lead to inaccurate answers.
assets.availability_impact: Loss or unavailability would reduce the assistant's ability to answer questions accurately.

assets.name: Embeddings index
assets.description: Vector embeddings and associated metadata for help-center articles and resolved support tickets stored in the managed retrieval index.
assets.confidentiality_impact: Embeddings may encode information from underlying tickets and documentation; compromise could leak patterns or approximate content across workspaces.
assets.integrity_impact: Corrupted embeddings or metadata could return incorrect passages or cross-tenant content.
assets.availability_impact: Loss or unavailability would prevent the assistant from retrieving relevant passages to answer questions.

assets.name: Workspace tokens
assets.description: Workspace-scoped bearer tokens representing signed-in users, used by the Relay Answers API to identify the caller's workspace, with candidate records describing development tokens and configuration fallbacks.
assets.confidentiality_impact: Exposure could allow impersonation of a workspace and unauthorized use of the assistant on that workspace's data.
assets.integrity_impact: Token misuse could allow unauthorized actions to appear as originating from a legitimate workspace.
assets.availability_impact: Loss or misconfiguration could prevent authorized workspaces from using the assistant.

assets.name: Answer analytics telemetry
assets.description: Telemetry records containing request identifiers, retrieved chunk text, and generated answers sent to the external analytics collector.
assets.confidentiality_impact: Telemetry may include ticket-derived text and answer content; exposure at the collector could leak sensitive customer information and configuration snippets.
assets.integrity_impact: Tampering with telemetry could distort operational analysis and any downstream processes relying on analytics.
assets.availability_impact: Loss of telemetry would reduce observability into assistant behavior but would not directly affect core answering functionality.

data_flows.name: Support platform export to ingestion pipeline
Provider wrapper to hosted model provider

trust_boundaries.name: Support platform export boundary
trust_boundaries.description: Boundary between Relay Answers ingestion and the external support platform that stores tickets, enforces a two-year retention schedule, and masks email addresses before export.

trust_boundaries.name: Managed vector database boundary
trust_boundaries.description: Boundary between internal ingestion processes and the managed vector database that stores embeddings and is reachable only from the answer service's network segment.

trust_boundaries.name: Model provider boundary
trust_boundaries.description: Boundary between the Relay Answers deployment and the hosted model provider API, which receives questions and retrieved passages over TLS and whose terms exclude training on submitted content.

trust_boundaries.name: Analytics collector boundary
trust_boundaries.description: Boundary between the internal provider wrapper and the external analytics collector that receives telemetry including retrieved chunk text and generated answers.

questions.question: Does the retrieval layer scope searches by workspace so that a workspace's queries cannot retrieve chunks originating from other workspaces, or does it currently operate as a process-global top-k search as described in the Mantis candidate record B.2?
questions.rationale: The architecture describes a single shared retrieval index serving all workspaces, and the Mantis packet's candidate record B.2 (evd-015) describes RetrievalIndex.search as operating over a process-global index without authorization scoping. Whether searches are scoped by workspace materially affects cross-tenant data exposure and is necessary to interpret the multi-tenant risk of the current design.

questions.question: What retention and reconciliation mechanism governs ticket-derived embeddings in the retrieval index, particularly in cases of partial or interrupted exports and deleted or corrected tickets?
questions.rationale: Primary documentation specifies a two-year retention period for resolved tickets on the support platform (evd-004) but does not describe how long ticket-derived embeddings are retained in the retrieval index. The Mantis candidate record B.3 (evd-015) suggests partial exports might leave stale chunks indefinitely. Clarifying the intended and actual retention and reconciliation behavior is important for assessing long-term storage of customer data in the index.

questions.question: Is the analytics collector at analytics.relay-answers.example enabled in production for Relay Answers traffic, and what data-handling and retention terms apply to the ticket-derived text and answers sent there?
questions.rationale: The main architecture and operations documents do not mention any external analytics processor, but the Mantis candidate record B.7 (evd-015) describes provider.py posting retrieved chunk text and generated answers to an external analytics collector. Confirming whether this collector is in scope for production deployments and documenting its data-handling terms is necessary to understand where customer support data flows and how it is protected.

questions.question: Does the production configuration for Relay Answers still include the fallback that activates hard-coded development workspace tokens when WORKSPACE_TOKENS is unset or empty, and if not, how is this guarded or validated at startup?
questions.rationale: The Mantis candidate record B.4 (evd-015) describes a configuration path where missing WORKSPACE_TOKENS causes load_settings to substitute predictable development tokens without a development-mode gate. Whether this behavior is present in production determines how configuration errors affect authentication and workspace isolation.
